name: Ray Charles
hook: A blind pianist who put a gospel song's shape under a secular love song in 1954, one of the records later counted among the first soul music, and who later won ownership of his own master tapes.
blurb: Ray Charles was born in Albany, Georgia, on 23 September 1930 and grew up in Greenville, Florida. He was blind by the age of seven, probably from glaucoma. In 1952 Ahmet Ertegun signed him to Atlantic Records in New York. In the summer of 1954 he heard a gospel song on the radio while on tour, the Southern Tones' 'It Must Be Jesus', and used its shape for 'I Got a Woman', a song about a girlfriend instead of God, recorded on 18 November 1954 at the Atlanta studio of the radio station WGST. At first he claimed he wrote it alone. Some church people were upset, but mixing church music with love songs became the basis of soul music, and Wikipedia's article on the song calls it one of the first examples of what was later called soul. In 1959 'What'd I Say', mixing gospel, jazz, blues and Latin rhythm, was his first big pop hit, in the top ten. When he moved to the ABC-Paramount label around 1959 and 1960, he got a deal in which he would eventually own his master recordings, which was unusual for any artist then and almost unheard of for a Black musician. 'Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music' (1962) took country songs into R&B and mainstream pop. He died in Beverly Hills on 10 June 2004.
